 Judgment

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.6,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 11.12.2020.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 11.12.2020 at about 10.00am, while the Petitioner was proceeding in a Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA54Q0313 as a pillion rider which was being ridden by its rider one Shivarajanna on Turuvekere Kadaballi Road in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, while they reached in front of Kadaballi Government School, Bindiganavile Hobli, Mandya, though there was a hump Shivrajanna did not slowdown the scooter, due to which the petitioner fell on the left side of the Road and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sparsha Hospital, Mysore Raod, Channarayapattana, Hassan District, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient, underwent surgeries and after necessary treatment discharged with an advice for follow up treatment.

So far he has spent huge amount towards surgery and medical expenses,
nourishment and transportation expenses.

4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy,
working in Coconut godown, earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
Due to the injuries till today the petitioner cannot attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning, earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.

The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA54Q0313 and the Bindiganavile police have filed charge sheet against the rider in Cr.No.94/2020 punishable u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statements.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, placed exparte.

6. The objections of the Respondent No.2:

sentences.text: It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of the policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of the Two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA54 Q0313.

It has contended that the said policy is a Two Wheeler Policy Bundled with coverage of risk own damage and compulsory personal accident to owner driver for the first year and the third party risk for Five years.
However, the respondent No.1 has not paid additional premium to cover the risk of pillion rider of a motorcycle as on the date of accident and hence this petition itself is not maintainable.
The petition is also not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have an effective and valid DL.

The Respondent insurer has further denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age, occupation,
income and other details of the Petitioner and has sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 11.12.2020 at 10.00 am due to rash and negligent riding of rider of Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA54Q0313 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?
3. What order or award?
8. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 11 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
He has also examined Mr.Rohith Kumar - MRO as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to P.15.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.16 & 17.

On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has got examined Mr. Vishal Kumar V. Paradeshi  Assistant Manager as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
9.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

10. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 11. Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA54Q0313 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
He has also examined MRO as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 to 15.

During the cross Guruprasad vs A.J.Kantharaj on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114205482/
3 examination of PW.1, he has stated that the vehicle number is corrected in Ex.P.13,
vehicle number appears to be 0313 whereas in the case sheet the vehicle number is mentioned as 8852.

sentences.text: 12 . The FIR was registered on the next day of accident i.e., on 12.12.2020 on the complaint of petitioner at Ex.P.1.
Ex . P.2
is the complaint lodged on 12.12.2020.
Ex . P.4
vehicle seizure mahazar conducted on 11.01.2021 and the vehicle seized between 2.00pm to 2.30pm.
Ex.P.5 MVA report shows that the vehicle damaged to its front left side panel shield guard, left side body shield panel guard, left side rear footrest scratched.
Ex . P.8
is the discharge summary shows that the petitioner underwent surgery of CRIF and ILN to his left leg.
Ex . P.7
is the charge sheet filed against the rider of the motorcycle after thorough investigation.
The respondent No.2 did not produce any document nor examined any witness in support of their contention to prove the negligence of the petitioner.
The corrections made in Ex.P.13 does not show the noninvolvement of the vehicle.
Therefore the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA54Q0313.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.16 & 17 clinical report and one Xray .
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and has stated about the physical disability of right lower limb at 42%, and to the whole body disability 14%.

14. During the cross examination of PW.3, he has admitted that it is wrongly mentioned that the petitioner has suffered right leg both bones fracture whereas the petitioner has suffered only fracture of right tibia.
15. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident he was working in Coconut Godown and earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
From the evidence of PW.3 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact his work.
Therefore, the court deems it fit to consider the whole body disability at 14%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working at Coconut Godown and getting salary of Rs.15,000/ per month.
However, he has not examined his employer nor produced any documents in support of it.
The accident occurred in the year 2020.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.14,500/ per month.
17. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 18 years as could be made out from Ex.P.9/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2020.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Sparsha Hospital,
Bangalore as an inpatient from 11.12.2020 to 15.12.2020, discharged with advice to take follow up Guruprasad vs A.J.Kantharaj on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114205482/
4 treatment.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.8 Discharge summary.
Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent huge amount towards hospitalization, medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for a sum of Rs.57,134/.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 5 days at Sparsh Hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.8 Discharge summary.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.14,500/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
On perusal of Ex.P.9, date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.2003 and the date of accident is 11.12.2020.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 18 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.
As such the petitioner is entitled to Rs.4,38,480/.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 18 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 14% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted for 5 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head.

(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

sentences.text: As per the version of PW.3, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implant, the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.3 have not produced any estimation bills.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.40,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.57,134/
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.14,500/
4. Loss of future income Rs.4,38,480/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.6,10,114/
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.6,10,200/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 19.
The Respondent No.2 has contended that since it was a bundled policy it did not have coverage for pillion rider.

In order to prove the same, it has got examined their Assistant Manager as RW.1,
who filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination reiterating the objections.
He got marked Exs.R.1 & 2 authorization letter and insurance policy.
During the crossexamination of RW.1, he has admitted that the accident occurred within one year of issuance of policy.
On perusal of Policy at Ex.R.2 it is clear that it is a bundled policy with own damage and personal accident coverage.

It is pertinent to refer to the following decisions:
(i) (2013) 1 Supreme Court Cases 731 : National Ins.
Co. Ltd., Vs. Balakrishnan & Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that a comprehensive/package policy would cover the liability of the insurer for payment of compensation for the occupant in a Car and an Act policy stands on a different footing which does not cover a Third Party risk of an occupant in a Car.

6 (ii) MFA 3178/2010 : United India Ltd., Vs. Shamaraya & Ors.

entities.text: MFA 3178/2010 : United India Ltd., Vs. Shamaraya & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that an Act policy/Statutory Policy/liability only policy covers the risk of Third Parties and if the insured wishes to cover the risk of occupants in the Car/Jeep or pillion rider in the motorcycle or damage caused to the vehicle, he has to pay higher amount for a Comprehensive Policy or a Package Policy.
Considering the definitions enshrined in Sec.2(33) and Sec.2(35) and Sec.147 of MV Act and if they are read harmoniously, the occupants/passengers/ inmates of a Private vehicle do not fall within the definition of category of Third Party.
(iii) 2018 SC 189 : Jagtar Singh alias jagdev Singh Vs. Sanjeev Kumar and Ors.

entities.text: Jagtar Singh alias jagdev Singh Vs. Sanjeev Kumar and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that liability of insurance companies in respect of occupance or gratuitious passengers in a private car depends on whether the policy is a comprehensive policy/package policy or whether it is just an act policy.
(iv) MFA No.188/2017 C/w 637/2018 :National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Praveen Cutinha and Anr.

entities.text: National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Praveen Cutinha and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that the premium paid would determine the nature of the coverage of policy.
The second construction is, when the word package/comprehensive is used that 'everything including the occupant, driver, owners, are covered under the policy'.
The premium paid is irrelevant and received to oblivion.

(v) MFA No.23416/2013 : M.Dada Khalander Vs. Muneer Khan and Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that in case of comprehensive or package policy, in a two wheeler, it covers the pillion rider and of a private car covers the occupants.

entities.text: M.Dada Khalander Vs. Muneer Khan and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, since the policy is a comprehensive package policy it also means that the pillion rider is covered.
Therefore, the Respondents being the Owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.6,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,10,200/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.6,10,200/ (Rupees Six Guruprasad vs A.J.Kantharaj on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114205482/
7 Lakhs Ten Thousand and Two Hundred only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
